title: Regional retention routing matrix and customer blocklist
creator: Lena Morris
description: Goal: Define and implement a canonical routing matrix that enforces EU data residency and retention constraints while supporting customer-scoped blocklists (blocklist = explicit customer/tenant prohibition for specific regions or tiers). This ticket covers schema, runtime enforcement points (API gateway, routing layer, and model-serving adapters), operator controls, and migration of existing customer mappings. We must support: 1) 'EU-only' customers (requests must stay inside EU regions), 2) residency-preferred customers (prefer EU but can failover under operator-approved conditions), 3) blocklisted customers that cannot be routed to specific tiers or regions, and 4) mapping to model variants for fallback (e.g., quantized local variant vs hosted large variant). This spec must be implementable in hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Routing matrix schema defined and documented in Confluence with examples covering all four customer policies.
A2: Runtime enforcement implemented: requests for 'EU-only' customers are rejected or routed to EU-local model variants; audit log entries emitted for every routing decision.
A3: Admin APIs to add/remove entries from the customer blocklist with RBAC gates and audit trail.
A4: Fallback policy ordering deterministic and documented (region affinity -> tier routing -> model-variant fallback -> operator override).
A5: End-to-end integration tests and chaos tests validate no cross-EEA egress for 'EU-only' under normal and partial-failure scenarios.
A6: Migration utility created to import existing mappings and a runbook for customer-facing communications.
A7: Telemetry dashboards show per-customer routing outcomes, blocked attempts, and fallback counts.
A8: Security review completed and approved prior to release to runtime-1.22.
A9: Performance regression <5% tail latency at 99th when enforcement is active (measured on staging).
implementation_plan: Design: finalize routing matrix schema (constrained YAML/JSON) and operator UI mapping in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Regional+Retention+Routing+Matrix
Runtime: implement enforcement hooks at routing proxy (pre-routing), policy engine (policy-evaluator service), and model adapter (final check).
Admin API: extend operator API to manage blocklist entries + web console form + RBAC checks.
Model mapping: create a lightweight registry table mapping customer -> allowed_regions -> allowed_tiers -> fallback_variants.
Migration: write migration script to translate existing geofencing tags into routing matrix rows with manual verification step.
Tests: unit, integration, and chaos testing (simulate EU region failure and validate fallback behavior).
Docs: operator runbook, customer-facing FAQ, and internal PRD links.
Deploy: staged rollout: canary on staging -> beta customers -> gradual prod rollout with monitoring and kill-switch.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Deploy policy-evaluator on staging and route 1% of traffic through new enforcement (2 days).
Stage 2 (internal beta): Enable enforcement for internal customers and 3 pilot customers in EU-only and residency-preferred tiers (7 days).
Stage 3 (gradual prod): 25% of affected customers, monitor for blocked legitimate traffic and latency regressions (14 days).
Stage 4 (full): Flip enforcement to 100% for configured customers. Keep operator kill-switch for 48 hours post-flip.
telemetry_and_metrics: Per-customer routing outcome count (allowed / blocked / fell back).
Per-region egress attempts for EU-only customers (should be zero).
Fallback model variant usage and latency delta vs primary variant.
Audit log volume and size per minute for high-volume customers.
Errors introduced by policy-evaluator and 5xx rates at routing proxy.
risks: False positives: overly strict blocklist rules could cause customer-facing errors; mitigations include dry-run mode and a detailed whitelist for testing customers.
Operational complexity: migrating thousands of customers may require manual verification and customer coordination.
Performance: policy checks add CPU and latency; must ensure caching of resolved policies reduces overhead.
Cross-environment differences: Private/VPC installs may have different region naming conventions; provide mapping layer.
Compliance ambiguity: some customers have mixed legal requirements; require legal signoff for 'residency-preferred' fallback rules.
notes: Related tickets: ENG-41875 (policy-evaluator infra), ENG-42012 (audit-log schema changes).
